entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-ccrj-gw8r-854m: opentelemetry-java: Quadratic CPU consumption in W3C tracestate parsing
entry.content:
opentelemetry-java: Quadratic CPU consumption in W3C tracestate parsing

Aliases: CVE-2026-118259

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-api — fixed in 1.67.0

### Summary OpenTelemetry Java's W3C trace-context propagator permits excessive CPU consumption when extracting crafted `tracestate` headers, potentially leading to denial of service. Regex backtracking causes quadratic parsing time for headers containing long runs of spaces or tabs without a following comma. ### Impact An unauthenticated attacker whose headers reach `W3CTraceContextPropagator.extract()` can cause excessive CPU usage through crafted requests. Parsing blocks the calling thread, potentially affecting other connections when extraction runs on a shared event-loop thread. Actual impact depends on ingress header-size limits, proxy configuration, and threading. Header-size limits reduce the per-request cost but do not eliminate the vulnerability. ### Patches Upgrade `io.open…

It is widely deployed in enterprise environments as a central authentication gateway. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-2vg8-q4c2-5cw3: OpenAM has LDAP Injection via `_queryId` Parameter
entry.content:
OpenAM has LDAP Injection via `_queryId` Parameter

Aliases: CVE-2026-41573

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • org.openidentityplatform.openam:openam-core-rest — fixed in 16.1.1

OpenAM (Open Identity Platform) is an open-source IAM platform providing SSO, OAuth2, SAML, and OpenID Connect capabilities. The CREST REST API layer exposes user query endpoints under `/json/{realm}/users`. In `IdentityResourceV1.queryCollection()`, the HTTP query parameter `_queryId` is passed to a `CrestQuery` object with `escapeQueryId` **explicitly set to `false`**, bypassing the escape protection introduced as part of the CVE-2021-29156 fix. The unescaped value flows directly to `DJLDAPv3Repo.getFilter()` where it is concatenated into an LDAP filter string without sanitization, enabling authenticated attackers to inject arbitrary LDAP metacharacters for user enumeration and blind LDAP injection. ## Affected Endpoint | Endpoint | Auth Required | Injection Parameter | |----------|---…

`jackson-databind`'s `PolymorphicTypeValidator` (PTV) is the primary safety mechanism guarding polymorphic deserialization. The nested type arguments are then resolved, instantiated, and populated as beans during deserialization. An attacker who controls the type ID can therefore pla…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-xqrx-qh46-34m7: snappy-java: JVM crash from unchecked ranges in Snappy.arrayCopy and SnappyOutputStream.rawWrite
entry.content:
snappy-java: JVM crash from unchecked ranges in Snappy.arrayCopy and SnappyOutputStream.rawWrite

Aliases: CVE-2026-116590

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.xerial.snappy:snappy-java — fixed in 1.1.10.9

### Impact `Snappy.arrayCopy(Object src, int offset, int byteLength, Object dest, int destOffset)` called a native `memcpy` without validating the ranges. A negative or oversized `byteLength` or offset read or wrote outside the arrays and crashed the JVM. `SnappyOutputStream.rawWrite` and `SnappyInputStream.rawRead`, and therefore the typed-array `write`/`read` methods, pass caller-supplied ranges to this method. ### Patches Fixed in 1.1.10.9 (#741). `Snappy.arrayCopy` checks both ranges before copying. The stream `read`/`write` methods validate offsets and lengths, and reject typed-array ranges whose byte size overflows `int`. ### Workarounds Validate offsets and lengths before calling these methods.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-gwq9-9ffj-mvrv: snappy-java: Heap buffer overflow in Snappy.uncompress*Array typed-array methods
entry.content:
snappy-java: Heap buffer overflow in Snappy.uncompress*Array typed-array methods

Aliases: CVE-2026-93451

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.xerial.snappy:snappy-java — fixed in 1.1.10.9

### Impact `Snappy.uncompressCharArray`, `uncompressShortArray`, `uncompressIntArray`, `uncompressLongArray`, `uncompressFloatArray` and `uncompressDoubleArray` sized the result array by dividing the declared uncompressed byte length by the element size, but native code wrote the full byte length. If the declared length is not a multiple of the element size, up to 7 bytes are written past the end of the Java array, corrupting the heap. ### Patches Fixed in 1.1.10.9 ([#739](https://github.com/xerial/snappy-java/pull/739)). These methods now reject uncompressed lengths that are not a multiple of the element size with `SnappyIOException`. ### Workarounds Check that `Snappy.uncompressedLength(input)` is a multiple of the element size before calling these methods.

# CompactHashMap/CompactHashSet/MapMakerInternalMap native deserialization triggers uncontrolled memory allocation ## Summary `CompactHashMap`, `CompactHashSet`, and `MapMakerInternalMap` implement `readObject(ObjectInputStream)` by reading an attacker-controlled `elementCount` or `initialCapacity` from the stream. On the very first insertion during or after deserialization (for the `CompactHash*` collections, inside `allocArrays()`) or immediately during deserialization (for `MapMakerInternalMap`), the implementation eagerly allocates arrays sized to that full, unvalidated value (up to `CompactHashing.MAX_SIZE` = 2^30-1, ~1.07 billion, for example) before the rest of the stream's actual content has been consumed.
